## Source and method

- https://developer.apple.com/documentation/healthkit

Every identifier in HealthKit's four naming families — HKQuantityTypeIdentifier, HKCategoryTypeIdentifier, HKCharacteristicTypeIdentifier and HKWorkoutActivityType — read on 2026-10-02 from the JSON Apple serves to render developer.apple.com. The identifier, Objective-C constant, group, abstract and platform versions are copied from Apple's payload unchanged. Two columns are DERIVED because Apple states them only in prose and not as machine-readable properties: aggregation (cumulative vs discrete) and unitFamily. Both are matched literally against Apple's own sentences — "measure cumulative values", "use energy units" — and are null where Apple's wording does not state them, never guessed. Both apply ONLY to quantity types: for the other three families they are null because the concept does not exist, not because Apple declined to state it — read them together with the family column. Aggregation is included because it determines whether HKStatisticsQuery should use .cumulativeSum or a discrete option, and choosing wrong returns a plausible wrong number rather than an error. valueEnum names the HKCategoryValue enum that decodes a category sample, which is null for every other family. Deprecation is read from Apple's availability data: a type counts as deprecated when any platform entry carries a deprecatedAt version, because Apple leaves its separate deprecated flag false even on deprecated symbols, and the iOS version, Apple's own deprecation note and any renamed-to target are published beside it. Apple's abstracts are reproduced for identification of the API surface; the analysis and the aggregation classification are this site's.

## Fields

| Field | Description | JSON types | Null in |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | Swift case name within its family | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `objcConstant` | The equivalent Objective-C constant | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `family` | Which of the four HealthKit identifier types this is a case of | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `group` | Apple's own topic grouping for the type | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `abstract` | Apple's one-line description, verbatim; null where Apple ships none | null, string | 5 of 241 rows |
| `aggregation` | DERIVED, quantity types only: cumulative or discrete per Apple's prose; null where unstated or not applicable | null, string | 124 of 241 rows |
| `unitFamily` | DERIVED, quantity types only: the unit family Apple names in prose | null, string | 125 of 241 rows |
| `valueEnum` | Category types only: the HKCategoryValue enum that decodes the sample | null, string | 213 of 241 rows |
| `iosIntroduced` | iOS version the type was introduced in | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `watchosIntroduced` | watchOS version the type was introduced in | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `deprecated` | yes when any platform entry in Apple's availability data carries a deprecatedAt version (or Apple's deprecated flag, which Apple leaves false even on deprecated symbols) | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `iosDeprecated` | iOS version Apple says the type was deprecated in; null when not deprecated on iOS | null, string | 237 of 241 rows |
| `deprecationNote` | Apple's deprecation note, verbatim, with symbol links resolved to their names; null where Apple gives none | null, string | 237 of 241 rows |
| `renamedTo` | The symbol Apple's availability data says the type was renamed to; null where Apple names none | null, string | 240 of 241 rows |
| `appleDocumented` | no when Apple ships the type with neither abstract nor discussion | string | 0 of 241 rows |
| `appleDocs` | Apple's reference page for the type — the page the row was read from, under the type's own family path | string | 0 of 241 rows |

A null means the source does not state the value or it could not be verified. It never means zero, and it is never a guess. In the CSV a null is an empty unquoted field.

## Update cadence

- `src/data/healthkitIdentifiers.ts` is generated by `scripts/fetch-healthkit-identifiers.mjs` from the sources above, last read 2026-10-02.
- No workflow runs that script: it is run by hand when the sources are re-read.
- The files are rebuilt by `npm run datasets` (scripts/build-datasets.mjs); a run with no source change writes byte-identical files. The edition stays 2026.1, and a new edition ships under a new file name rather than overwriting this one.
